title: the identity counts the file's claim or an accepted statement
line: a page anyone can edit is taken on the name and three of birth day, death day, burial place and a stated parent or spouse, each claimed or accepted, a claim the file cites to that very page not among them: Helen Sara Brant's gravestone, read, is taken by the rule on her name and birth day, both her own word, and gives her death day; once that decision is withdrawn its statements stand undecided, neither the file's claim nor accepted, so her memorial, whose death day the tree has only from them and whose burial only from a claim citing the memorial itself, agrees on her birth day and her father alone and is refused, its reason naming what it left out

steps.say: the owner's word on Helen's name and birth day; the file's claims of her death set aside

fact.note: harness: the file's death set aside

steps.say: her gravestone's photograph, archived under its memorial's photographs
the stone read, typed by the harness in the model's place from the image's own words (AHEARN over her panel: HELEN BRANT, JULY 11 1909, JAN 24, 1986): taken by the rule on her name and birth day

expect.why: a gravestone's photograph once read is a kind the rule takes: her name and her birth day, her own word, agree

steps.say: the rule's decision on the stone withdrawn: its statement of her death day stands undecided
her memorial, a page anyone can edit: born and died on the stone's days, buried at Methacton, her parents and her husband listed

has: here birth date to the day, parent
not counted: death date to the day, which the tree has only from a statement left undecided
burial place, which the tree has only from a claim citing this very page

expect.why: a statement a withdrawal left undecided is neither the file's claim nor accepted: the birth day and her father are two of the four
